first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Both memory_31 and memory_86 show that signup/onboarding simplification directly improved activation metrics in earlier tests. This is the most direct lever for the dual decline we're seeing. Verifying these two memories will confirm the magnitude and durability of the effect before committing. Promotional pricing addresses competitor entry but risks commoditization of our value prop and could cannibalize full-price customers. Referral incentives work best on *established* customers (memory_57) when we need to recover *new* customer activation. Enterprise sales assist is orthogonal to the immediate SMB activation crisis. Simplifying onboarding has the lowest downside risk and highest relevance to current performance gaps. A standard experiment gives us statistical confidence while preserving the option to iterate or pivot if results disappoint.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. exp_31 showed signup simplification lifted SMB activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% with minimal retention risk (-1%). exp_86 showed shortened onboarding lifted completion +13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention +3%. Current state shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—precisely the metrics these interventions have proven to move. The verified effect sizes are substantial and retention-safe. Promotional pricing would address competitor pressure but risks margin erosion on price-sensitive cohorts we may retain through better activation. Referral incentives depend on established customer base strength which we should first stabilize. Simplifying onboarding has the strongest evidence base, lowest execution risk, and fastest path to recovering activation metrics. Standard experiment scope allows statistical validation while preserving urgency. Running this week captures the activation decline while it's still recoverable.
